rows.medi_said: I really need the word for motivated.
rows.amal_said: We know motivation حافز أو دافع. ... a good word for motivated is متشجع.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'motivated' and Amal supplied متشجع.
He used شجاع (brave) for 'motivated'; Amal had just taught متشجع and recast it at once.
After متشجع the word takes la- not 3ashaan; Amal said لا and 'It takes لا'.
He meant 'I drove for two hours' (her chat su2et); he kept saying سويت (I did) and she voiced a su2et-like word (engine wrote صرت/سألت).

rows.medi_said: أنا كنت بهمس. أنا كنت أهمس.
rows.why: He turned the adjective متحمس into a made-up present verb; Amal recast to كنت متحمس.

rows.amal_said: سجادة. ... بعت أكتر من عشرين سجادة.
rows.why: After 11+ the noun is singular سجادة, not the collective سجاد; repeated at 09:49 and 10:05, one row.

rows.medi_said: How do I say customers I was excited for?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'excited for them'.
She taught 'excited for them' = متحمس إلهم; he said إنهم and she recast to إلهم.

rows.medi_said: جيب. It would be جابت؟ بجيب، جابت.
rows.why: Past of بجيب for 'I' is جبت (short e), not جابت; Amal recast and explained 'E's turn into short E's'.

rows.amal_said: ما؟ They are a group so they didn't.
rows.why: Customers are plural so the verb needs the -u 'they' ending; Amal prompted and he fixed to ما شطارو.
He said a plural/wrong form مواعد; Amal recast the singular موعد.

rows.amal_said: So we say من الأسبوع الماضي.
rows.chat: ana jahhazet la-ijtimaa3/maw3ed min el-usboo3 el-maadi
rows.why: He left out the preposition من ('since'); Amal supplied it.

rows.chat: ana jahhazet la-ijtimaa3/maw3ed min el-usboo3 el-maadi
rows.why: He dropped el- from the noun while keeping it on the adjective; her own line and chat have el-usboo3 el-maadi; she let it pass.

rows.amal_said: شافت. ... So I showed is a different verb.
rows.why: He used شفت (I saw) for 'I showed'; Amal said 'I showed is a different verb' (sheet: i showed | Ana farjait | أنا فرجيت).
rows.english: when I showed her the rug

rows.why: 'I showed her' needs the object ending on the verb; Amal recast فرجته/فرجتها.
For 'fun' he said بيضحكوا (they're funny); Amal flagged the meaning and he moved to بيبسطوا / بيسلوا.

rows.amal_said: Where do I put the L? Those expensive dresses.
rows.why: After هدول the noun keeps el-; Amal prompted and he fixed to هدول الفساتين.
He gave the singular for 'long trips'; Amal repeated 'Long trips' and he fixed to the plural safrat el twaal.
She asked for 'that young guy'; he said zalameh (man) and she re-prompted 'young man', he switched to shab.
العيلة is feminine singular so it takes هادي not هدول; Amal repeated 'This family' and he fixed to هادي العيلة.
For 'is amazing' he put ما in front, which negates it; her chat has betjannen with no ma; could be a filler.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Both sides arrive or reach. ... it's basour.
rows.why: For 'visited us' he used a وصل-like verb (arrive); Amal said No and pointed him to بزور (sheet: i visit | Ana bazoor | أنا بزور).

rows.amal_said: There's a big table. Do I need L here?
rows.why: An indefinite noun + adjective takes no el- on the adjective; Amal prompted and he dropped it.
باب is masculine so the adjective is مفتوح; Amal recast twice and he named the reason (it's bab).

rows.medi_said: So el ba-- No. Yeah, el bab.
rows.why: In idafa the first noun never takes el-; Amal said 'No ال' and he fixed to bab al-ghurfa al-maftuh.

rows.medi_said: I forgot the word for, like, mild sickness.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'sick' and Amal supplied عيانة.

rows.medi_said: walad al, uh, ayan. ... walad al ayan
rows.amal_said: So where do I put the ال؟ ... No. ... It's the sick boy.
rows.chat: el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito
rows.why: 'The sick boy' needs el- on both noun and adjective; Amal said No until he said الولد العيان.

rows.chat: el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito
rows.why: After laazem the verb drops b-; Amal repeated لازم and he said يدل.

rows.chat: el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito
rows.why: 'Stay home' needs في, not على or nothing; Amal said 'In his home' and he fixed to في بيته.

rows.amal_said: ممتاز. So for feminine nouns, what do we add?
rows.why: A feminine first word in idafa takes -t (sayyaaret); after ممتاز she asked what feminine nouns add and he answered 'T'.

rows.amal_said: the apple tree. I'm not describing the tree. I'm saying it's the tree of apples.
rows.why: He started el-shajar el-... (noun + adjective); Amal said it is idafa ('the tree of apples'), later شجرة التفاح.

rows.amal_said: ليش فيه هون؟ ... No, they're just هون. طلاب الجامعة هون.
rows.why: 'Are here' needs no word; فيه means 'there is'; Amal said No and gave طلاب الجامعة هون.

rows.medi_said: was it bar? ... Jazam. ... I forgot.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he could not find 'suitcase' and Amal supplied شنتة سفر.
He used the MSA-shaped form يصلوا; Amal recast to her dialect يوصلوا (sheet: i arrive | Ana bawsal | أنا بوصل).
